proposal_nominal.check: House equity 700,000 + cash 50,000 + Volvo 20,000 = 770,000. 401(k) 400,000 + brokerage 300,000 + cash 50,000 + Tacoma 20,000 = 770,000. Schedule total 1,540,000 reconciles (1,100,000 - 400,000 mortgage + 400 + 300 + 100 + 20 + 20 = 1,540,000). Nominal equality is arithmetically correct as stated.

proposal_after_tax.assumptions: Each side valued net of taxes embedded in the assets it receives, sale/current value held constant. WIFE: house equity 700,000; eventual sale at today's value with 6% selling costs (66,000); amount realized 1,034,000 - carryover basis 300,000 (26 U.S.C. sec.1041) = gain 734,000; sec.121 single exclusion 250,000 -> taxable 484,000; tax at 15% LTCG + 3.8% NIIT = 18.8% (NIIT assumed per engagement convention because sale-year MAGI, 72,000 wages + 484,000 gain, far exceeds 200,000) = 90,992; net house equity 543,008. Plus cash 50,000 + Volvo 20,000 = 613,008. HUSBAND: 401(k) 400,000 pre-tax, taxed on withdrawal at his stated marginal rate 24% (engagement assumption; sensitivity: 12% -> 352,000, 32% -> 272,000) = 304,000; brokerage 300,000 with gain 80,000 (basis 220,000) taxed 18.8% = 15,040, net 284,960 (gain would be realized on sale; MAGI 218,400 incl. expected bonus exceeds 200,000 so NIIT applies); plus cash 50,000 + Tacoma 20,000 = 658,960. GAP: husband is 45,952 better off after tax, about 6.0% of the estate, because wife's package carries 156,992 of selling costs + tax (22.4% of house equity) vs husband's 111,040 (15.4% of the assets he takes). If wife never sells the house the gain is deferred, not avoided; a future sale at a higher price increases her tax.

undisclosed_income.source: Granite Peak HR letter dated 2026-03-02 (target bonus 45,000 for 2026, paid 50% September and 50% February 'on achievement of plan,' with employee currently at 112% of plan -> 45,000 x 1.12 = 50,400 expected 2026 bonus). Corroborated by 2026-09-15 pay stub: YTD gross 146,212 vs salary prorate 119,000 = 27,212 unexplained, consistent with the September installment of 22,500-25,200. The sworn affidavit (2026-08-30) states bonus 'discretionary; none expected for 2026,' contradicted by the employer letter written five months earlier. Client now adds (2026-10): Husband 'always gets a bonus,' and his 2025 bonus was approximately 40,000 - client recollection only, no 2025 employer documents in the file (flagged: unverified amount, but recurrence itself comes from the same party who negotiated the bonus plan language in the HR letter and is consistent with YTD stub excess). Recurrence evidence strengthens the guideline finding that bonuses are 'expected or recurring bonuses' and the Rule 16.2(e) case that the affidavit's 'none expected' was false when made. Floor 45,000 (target) if 112%-of-plan performance is not accepted; the February 2027 installment of the 2026 bonus (approx. 25,200) had not yet been paid at the affidavit date. assumption (flagged): work performed during marriage is treated as marital property, consistent with the parties' own schedule treating the 401(k), which 'accrued entirely during marriage,' as marital - the library does not define marital-vs-separate property.

alternatives.name: A. Original structure plus equalization payment to Wife
alternatives.description: House (equity 700,000) to Wife; Husband keeps 401(k) and brokerage; Husband concedes an additional 23,000 of cash/brokerage so post-tax outcomes equalize (total after-tax 1,271,968 / 2 = 635,984; Wife was short 22,976; 23,000 is the rounded transfer, hence the 24 difference between the two sides). Preserves the client's goal of keeping the house for the children.
instruments: Refinance of the 400,000 mortgage into Wife's name with pay-off of Husband's half of remaining liquid funds at closing
Quitclaim deed to Wife incident to decree (no gain under sec.1041)

Promissory note / staged payment if Husband's liquidity is short; alternatively Wife receives 23,000 from the 401(k) by QDRO (pre-tax; its after-tax value to Wife depends on her marginal ordinary rate, not stated in the library - unverified)

Refinance contingency (recommended in light of client's 2026-10 statement that she does not know whether she can qualify): decree orders house to Wife subject to her obtaining refinance approval within a fixed window (e.g., 90 days); Wife advises seeking pre-approval before signing; lender qualification standards are outside the library and unverified - the affordability arithmetic below is not underwriting

Fallback if the refinance window lapses: either Alternative B (sale while married, joint return) or Alternative D (deferred co-owned sale) - do NOT default to a quitclaim-to-Wife-then-forced-later-sale structure, which forfeits approx. 47,000 of sec.121 exclusion

alternatives.name: B. Sell the residence now, before the decree, on a joint return
alternatives.description: Sale while married with 500,000 sec.121 joint exclusion: gain 734,000 - 500,000 = 234,000 x 18.8% = 43,992 tax; net 590,008; each side 295,004 plus half of the other assets after embedded tax (401(k) half 200,000 x 76% = 152,000; brokerage half 150,000 - 40,000 gain x 18.8% = 142,480; cash 10,000; car 20,000) = 619,484 each. Joint exclusion saves 47,000 of tax (18.8% x the extra 250,000) versus Wife selling later as a single filer - but the children must move at separation and the parties must remain married and file jointly for the year of sale, contrary to the client's stated goal. Listed to quantify the trade-off, not recommended as drafted.
instruments: Listing/interim sale agreement executed before entry of decree (sec.121 500,000 exclusion requires a joint return)
No QDRO required absent any 401(k) transfer between the parties
Joint 2026 federal return (filing status fixed by marital status on Dec 31)

alternatives.name: C. Unequal division on grounds of nondisclosure (Rule 16.2(e))
alternatives.description: Not quantified: the statute (Col. R. Fam. P. 16.2(e) as set out in the library) authorizes reopening the judgment and sanctions for failure to disclose income 'including bonuses and expected compensation,' including an unequal division in favor of the non-disclosing party's opponent; the library states the remedy exists but gives no formula, so the amount of an enhanced award is unquantified here (unverified beyond the rule's text). Minimum concrete ask: add the September 2026 bonus installment already received (22,500 at target; 25,200 at 112% of plan) and the February 2027 installment (approx. 25,200) to the marital estate, and require accounting of the 27,212 YTD excess; demand the Rule 16.2(e) remedy for the affidavit's false statement. Client's 2026-10 statement that Husband 'always gets a bonus' (2025 approx. 40,000, client recollection) further corroborates recurrence.
instruments: Motion to compel corrected financial affidavit and production of bonus plan documents
Post-decree motion to reopen under Rule 16.2(e) if the false affidavit surfaces later

alternatives.name: D. Deferred co-owned sale (stay 3-6 years, both on title, then sell) - new fallback per client's 2026-10 goals
alternatives.description: If Wife cannot refinance, she does not have to sell now and does not have to eat a solo-filer tax bill later: both parties remain on title after the decree, Wife receives exclusive occupancy under the divorce instrument, and the house is sold when the children leave (3-6 years per client's goal). Reading the library's text of sec.121(b)(1) (250,000 individual exclusion) with sec.121(d)(3)(A) (an individual is treated as using the property as a principal residence during any period of ownership while the individual's spouse or former spouse is granted use under a divorce instrument): each former co-owner who still owns at sale may claim his or her own 250,000 exclusion, so the combined exclusion is 500,000 WITHOUT a joint return and WITHOUT staying married. Arithmetic at today's value: gain 734,000 (amount realized 1,034,000 - basis 300,000), split 367,000 per co-owner (this analysis assumes equal ownership shares; the decree must fix the split), each 367,000 - 250,000 = 117,000 taxable x 18.8% = 21,996, total 43,992; net 634,000 - 43,992 = 590,008; each 295,004 plus half of other assets after embedded tax = 619,484 each - identical to Alternative B's numbers, but sale occurs at children's exit instead of now, and Wife keeps the house in the interim. Same approx. 47,000 saving versus Wife owning alone at sale (66,000 selling costs and tax figures held at today's values; future value drift not modeled and cuts both ways; NIIT on a sale-year MAGI with 484,000+ of gain assumed as in the base case). Trade-offs (flagged): Husband remains on the mortgage and any refinance/assumption question disappears, but Wife's exclusive control ends; the divorce instrument must fix who pays the mortgage, taxes, insurance, and maintenance while co-owned (contribution tracking), an exit trigger and listing mechanics, and each side's right to sale proceeds; his continuing exposure to the loan is leverage for cooperation. Expense-sharing terms adjust each side's real recovery and are not priced here. The (d)(3)(A) use-inclusion reading is our application of the library's excerpted text and nothing in the library contradicts it.
instruments: Decree keeps both parties on title (no sec.1041 full transfer to Wife)
Exclusive-use/occupancy provision under the divorce instrument (invoke sec.121(d)(3)(A) for Husband deemed use; Wife qualifies by actual use plus ownership in all relevant 2-of-5-year periods)
Co-ownership expense-resolution: mortgage, property tax, insurance, repairs allocation; contribution ledger
Fixed-term buy-sell/exit agreement: children's exit triggers listing; or earlier options (either party may buy out the other at appraised value)

Deferred-sale order in form acceptable to both; each side's 250,000 exclusion requires status as owner + use within 2 of the 5 years before sale (satisfied per (d)(3)(A) for the non-occupant co-owner)

maintenance_tax_treatment: Husband's proposal to make the 2,000/month x 36 months 'deductible to Husband and taxable to Wife' is legally unavailable: for divorce or separation instruments executed after December 31, 2018 (all instruments executed now), alimony is neither deductible by the payor nor includible by the recipient (post-TCJA, per irc_1041_121_71.md), and child support is never deductible or includible. Consequence: Husband bears the full 72,000 with no offset - a fact his counsel's draft ignores and which supports asking whether 36 months is the right length; Wife receives the 72,000 tax-free, which is favorable to her and should not be traded away for a nominal 'gross-up.'
dependents_and_filing_status: If the decree is final on or before December 31, 2026, both parties file single or head of household for 2026 onward (marital status fixed at year-end; per filing_status_dependents.md). Wife is the custodial parent (approx. 70% of nights, above the 65% guideline line in columbia_child_support_guidelines.md): under IRC sec.152(e) the custodial parent claims the children unless she releases the claim on Form 8332 - Husband's 'alternating years' scheme requires Wife to sign a release each of his years, moving the child tax credit to him in those years. Head-of-household status, EITC, and the dependent-care credit cannot be transferred by Form 8332 (they stay with the custodial parent). Recommended position: Wife signs no Form 8332; if trade value is needed, release only the dependency/child tax credit by Form 8332 for specified years - never head-of-household or care credits (they do not transfer in any event). Whether Wife qualifies for head-of-household for 2026 requires that she pay more than half the cost of the home and a child lived with her more than half the year ( IRC sec.2(b)) - with the house transferring to her in 2026 and approx. 70% of nights, that is plausible but fact-dependent; unverified until the residence arrangement is set.
